2026-11-16: 63 -> 59. driver-portal's four unguarded duty writes are gone.

startDuty and endDuty both read the ACTIVE duty and then wrote COMPLETED
with a plain update. Two devices standing down at once therefore wrote two
different endedAt values onto one row and enqueued two driver.duty.completed
events carrying two different durations for one shift — and duty time is
what pay and compliance are worked out from. Two devices STARTING at once
was worse: both saw no active duty and both created one, leaving a driver
with two open shifts.

Both writes are now compare-and-set on status ACTIVE, and both take a
per-driver advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock, transaction-scoped) before
reading, so the read sees what an earlier serialised call committed. Where
the write matches nothing the caller is told the shift was already ended
rather than being handed a duration it never recorded.

Note the lock is what fixes the two-open-shifts case; compare-and-set alone
does not, because two inserts have nothing to compare against. The
structural fix — a partial unique index on driver_duties ("driverId")
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' — remains outstanding: Prisma cannot express a
partial index, so it would have to be hand-written and would then differ
from schema.prisma, which is why it was not done here.

driver-portal is not added to MUST_BE_CLEAN. Only the duty paths were
examined; the module still has unguarded status writes elsewhere.


2026-11-16: 65 -> 63. Route load and scan moved from
src/manifests/load-scan.controller.ts into load-scan.service.ts, and both of
its status writes became compare-and-set: the waybill transition is an
updateMany constrained on the expected current status, and dispatch is
constrained on dispatched = false. The controller now holds only the HTTP
shape, so a second operator scanning the same parcel and a second
completeLoad can no longer both report success for one physical event.

manifests is not added to MUST_BE_CLEAN. rail-manifest.service.ts still has
two unguarded status writes, and claiming the module was finished to make a
number go away is the thing this file exists to prevent.


Status writes that still read-then-write instead of compare-and-set. NO ROT holds the listed modules at zero; RATCHET holds the total to this number or lower. A hit is a place for a human to look, not a proven bug — some are guarded by an enclosing row lock. Re-record only after the count fell, and say how in the commit.
